purpose: The JS/TS history-replay corpus ruled on #212 on 2026-10-06: six JS/TS repositories, the last 300 non-merge commits of each (1,800 commits), run as consecutive whole-commit windows with `checkwash sweep`, the JS counterpart of the six-repository Python sweep
selection_reading: Each repository's package manifest and test-file paths at the pinned commit were read to confirm its runner and layout; no checkwash engine ran on any of them
selection_rule: Widely used, actively maintained open-source JS/TS projects whose test suites run under one of the runners the JS rounds read: Jest, Vitest, Mocha with chai, and node:test
Together they cover the test layouts the rounds read: tests colocated beside the source (`*.test.ts`), `__tests__/` directories and a `test/` directory
At least 300 non-merge commits reachable from the pinned commit
No repository checkwash has run on before (see `excluded`)

excluded.reason: Repositories the JS rounds, fixtures or replays have already run on, so their histories are in-sample

window: The 300 newest non-merge commits reachable from `commit`: `git rev-list --no-merges -300 <commit>`, each judged against its first parent as `checkwash sweep` does
class_note: In-sample or held-out (SPEC §10) is not ruled: #212's question 2 is asked again when the release that ships the JS rounds is prepared. No engine has run on these windows, so either label remains possible
release_criterion_note: #212's question 3, asked at the same time
engines_to_measure: The candidate of the release that ships the JS rounds, against v0.6.0, on the same windows (#212, acceptance 2)

repositories.runner_evidence: package.json: scripts.test runs `jest` with `config/jest.config.ts`, devDependencies `jest`, `ts-jest`, `@jest/globals`; tests beneath `__tests__/` directories (270 files)
package.json: dependency `vitest`; tests colocated beside the source as `src/**/*.test.ts` (160)
package.json: devDependency `borp`, a node:test runner; tests in `test/` call `require('node:test')` (514 files)
